newsitem.title: USA: Indianapolis creates new taxing district for arena.
newsitem.headline: Indianapolis creates new taxing district for arena.

text.p: Indianapolis City Council approved a special professional sports development district to back $50 million of bonds for a new arena to house the Indiana Pacers basketball team, a spokeswoman for Mayor Stephen Goldsmith said Tuesday.
The council voted 26-1 Monday night to approve the use of the district to capture state income and sales taxes in an area of downtown Indianapolis, spokeswoman Kate Healey said.
Indiana lawmakers had approved creation of the district during a special session last month.
The estimated $175 million cost of the arena includes funding of at least $104 million from private sources as well.
Pacers owners Herb and Melvin Simon will provide $57 million through ticket tax and parking revenues.
Another 16 investors in the Circle Centre Mall downtown have committed $3.7 million annually for debt service on $37 million of bonds for the arena also.
Eli Lilly & Co has pledged the use of land adjacent to the arena site valued at $10 million for parking and construction staging as well, Goldsmith said.

In addition to the sports development district, public financing plans include a $4.7 million infrastructure grant, $9.3 million of restricted reserves from the Capital Improvement Board and $7 million in revenues from the Circle Centre Mall designated for downtown development.
The arena is scheduled to open in fall 1999.
